ISSUE
Public Hearing to adopt Joint Resolution No. CC 2021-058, SA 2021-005, HA 2021-002,
IDA 2021-001, PAA 2021-001, PCA 2021-002 and PFA 2021-002, approving the
Biennial Operating and Capital Improvement Budget for Fiscal Years 2021-23.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council, Chairs, Commissioners, Members and
Directors conduct a public hearing to adopt Joint Resolution No. CC 2021-058, SA 2021-
005, HA 2021-002, IDA 2021-001, PAA 2021-001, PCA 2021-002 and PFA 2021-002,
approving the Biennial Operating and Capital Improvement Budget for Fiscal Years
2021-23.

BACKGROUND
Each year the City is required to adopt a budget for the operation of the City. The budget
serves as the City’s financial plan for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1 through June 30.
It defines City priorities for the provision of services to the community.

According to the Palmdale Municipal Code: Chapter 3.04 Budget Adoption Procedures,
the City Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May
31st of each year. Additionally, the City Council shall conduct a public hearing on the
proposed budget before adoption and shall adopt a budget prescribing the spending
policy of the City for the ensuing fiscal year on or before the thirtieth day of June of each
year.
 Report to Mayor and City Council, Chairs, Commissioners, Members, and Directors
Re: Proposed Biennial Budget FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23
June 15, 2021
Page 2

On May 12, 2021, the Library Board of Trustees reviewed the proposed budget made a
unanimous recommendation to the City Council to approve the proposed Library budget.

On May 13, 2021, the Planning Commission unanimously found that the proposed
Capital Improvement Program is consistent with the goals, objectives, and policies of
the General Plan.

On May 18, 2021, the City Council was presented with a draft of the proposed Biennial
Budget for Fiscal Years 2021-23.

On May 19, 2021, the Measure AV Oversight Committee reviewed the proposed budget
and made a unanimous recommendation to the City Council to approve the proposed
Measure AV Fund budget.

DISCUSSION
Today, Palmdale along with the rest of our nation, is emerging from one of the most
difficult periods in recent history. For over a year, the COVID-19 pandemic has dominated
our lives and has impacted everyone. Thankfully, as a result of protocols to reduce the
transmission and the advent of safe and effective vaccines, developed in record time,
infection rates have slowed dramatically, and life is beginning to return to normal.

However, COVID-19 brought with it a world-wide economic recession resulting in record
high unemployment, business closures and a precipitous drop-in economic activity.
Under the leadership of the Mayor and the City Council, staff were able to quickly respond
in a variety of ways to support the community during this tumultuous period.

In alignment with the City’s adopted Strategic Plan and Renaissance Plan, below is a list
of program highlights planned for FY 2022 and FY 2023:
    Palmdale Cares associated programs.
    Enhance food distribution programs at SAVES, Legacy Commons and other local
  charity-based organizations.
    Operation Jumpstart Part III.
    Reopening of Recreation Activities, Venues and Events.
    Continued rental and mortgage assistance.
    Community grants for organizations to further improve and enhance the quality of
  life.
    Continued Small Business Support Programs.
    Support programs for community partners.

    More investment into infrastructure.
    Enhanced staffing levels to manage new community service programs and
  projects to keep up with the needs of the City.

GENERAL FUND
Revenues
  1. Property Taxes are expected to increased by 2% due to property values
  increasing.
 Report to Mayor and City Council, Chairs, Commissioners, Members, and Directors
Re: Proposed Biennial Budget FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23
June 15, 2021
Page 4

  2. Sales Taxes are expected to increase by 5% according to our consultants and
  economic performance in the City.
  3. Charges for Services are expected remain reduced by $1.6 million as the City
  continues to make adjustments to restart events and activities. Staff is also aware
  that it is important to be sensitive to the population who is still vulnerable and
  concerned about COVID-19. However, in FY 2023, revenues rebound significantly
  to normal levels.
  4. Licenses and permits are expected to increase by $1.9 million next year as a result
  of two major developments potentially starting construction.
  5. Transfers In increased due to Measure AV funds in the amount of $7 million being
  used to maintain Public Works and Neighborhood Services Programs. American
  Rescue Funds are also being transferred in the amount of $2.4 million to cover the
  cost of lost revenue due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Expenditures
  1. Salaries and benefits are expected to increase by 5% (3% wage increase and 2%
  COLA) to employees.
  2. LA County Sheriff Contract is expected to increase by 1.45% or $1.2 million. In
  FY 2021, AVTA provided the City with $1.6 million for assistance with COVID
  compliance. The City will be responsible for the total contract in addition to the
  increase.
  3. LA County Sheriff Contract Liability is expected to remain the same at 11% of the
  contract, for an increase of $326,590.
  4. Transfers to Reserves include:
  a. Pension Trust Fund to stabilize fluctuations in CalPERS rates: $1.25 million
  b. Capital Improvement Fund to help fund miscellaneous projects with no other
  source of funding or matching for grants: $1 million
  c. Fleet Maintenance to fund the ongoing replacement of the City’s fleet:
  $250,000
  d. Information Technology: to fund the ongoing upgrade of the City’s
  technology infrastructure: $250,000
  e. Park Development Fund to establish health reserves in the event the City
  chooses to finance large projects in the future.

MEASURE AV
FY 2022 will be the first full year of generating revenue through Measure AV. Staff
anticipates generating approximately $15.5 million in revenue from the ¾ cent sales tax
passed by Palmdale voters in November 2020.
 Report to Mayor and City Council, Chairs, Commissioners, Members, and Directors

Expenditures
  1. Mental Health Programs - $300,000
  2. Community Partnerships - $300,000
  3. Administrative Costs to support administration of the fund such the Oversight
  Committee and staffing to implement and manage programs - $195,000
  4. SAVES – $150,000
  5. Emergency Management - $250,000
  6. Public Safety Enhancements and maintaining existing services - $7.9 million
  7. Community Compliance – Code enforcement enhancements $523,700
  8. Economic Development – initiatives to continue to support small businesses and
  Operation Jumpstart - $632,000

AMERICAN RESCUE FUNDS
Palmdale’s allocation is expected to be approximately $35.5 million.
Expenditures
  1. The City intends to launch a community sponsorship program to local
  organizations to implement programs or projects that will enhance the quality of
  life in Palmdale. $10 million has been budgeted in each year to fund these grants.
  2. Just over $1 million has been allocated to City facilities such as parks and the
  library to allow for increased educational opportunities for students as a result of
  schools and other public facilities being closed in response to the pandemic.
  3. The City is launching a marketing campaign “Film Palmdale” to encourage more
  of the industry to consider Palmdale as a site location in the future. This campaign
  is estimated to cost $250,000.
  4. Nearly $4.3 million has been identified to reimburse both the General Fund and
  Dry Town for lost revenues as a result of the pandemic closures.
  5. During the May 10, 2021 Joint City Council meeting with the City of Lancaster, the
  City Councils directed staff to collaborate on regional economic development
  activities. There is $125,000 set aside to work with AV Edge on a regional
  campaign to attract businesses and industries to the Antelope Valley.
  6. During the pandemic, internet accessibility was unreliable and scarce in the
  community. $125,000 has been set aside to continue the City’s efforts in
  expanding access throughout the region.

SPECIAL REVENUE
Gas Tax: The City has not received communication that the allocation to Palmdale will
be affected as a result of the pandemic.
Metro Transportation Tax: The City has not received communicated that the allocation
to Palmdale will be affected as a result of the pandemic.
SB1 Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Tax: The City has not received communicated
that the allocation to Palmdale will be affected as a result of the pandemic.
On pages 4-7 of the proposed budget schedules, projected revenues for the next two
years are presented along with the proposed operating and capital expenditures.

CONCLUSION
The proposed Biennial Budget is balanced and represents the City’s commitment to the
long term planning and sustainability of programs and services for the community. The
proposed budget is evaluated over two years to ensure that the decisions made today
are fiscally sustainable for the future.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Fiscal Year 2021-22 and Fiscal Year 2022-23 Operating Budget will serve as the
financial guidelines for program implementation for the year. The proposed biennial
budget is compliant with all Financial Policies, including the 20% General Fund Reserve
Requirement. It is anticipated that revenues will be sufficient to cover the expenditures
proposed.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  B. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.
  C. Involve and expand engagement to enhance public oversight and
  transparency.

“Adopted Biennial Budget for Fiscal Year 2021-22 and Fiscal Year 2022-23,” attached
hereto and incorporated herein by reference.

  SECTION 6. That the Chief Financial Officer/City Treasurer is authorized to
validate, sign and pay all legal and contractual obligations of the City, including City
Departments and agencies with check warrants up to the amounts appropriated in this
budget.

  SECTION 7. The Finance Manager shall have the authority to receive, up to
$50,000, on behalf of the City, any and all donations and make the appropriate entries
into the City financial records to enable the City to spend the donation on the purpose
for which it was intended without presenting each item to the City Council for approval.
These donations, received throughout the fiscal year by various departments from
members of the community for a variety of purposes, are obligated and not
discretionary. All donations more than such amount shall be approved by the City
Council, the Successor Agency to the Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of
Palmdale, the Palmdale Civic Authority, the Housing Authority, the Industrial
Development Authority, the Palmdale Airport Authority, and the Palmdale Financing
Authority.

  SECTION 8. That at the conclusion of fiscal year ending June 30, 2021, certain
purchase order will exist as outstanding encumbrances representing contractual
obligations or previously budgeted funds. In addition, budgeted funds for certain items
or projects in various stages of acquisition or development have previously been
approved or will be approved by City Council to be carried forward to fiscal year 2021-
22 as Continuing Appropriations. The Outstanding Encumbrances and Continuing
Appropriations shall be deemed to be re-budgeted as an addition to the budget
amounts previously set forth in the Resolution.

section 34176(d)), are necessary for the production, improvement or preservation of

  SECTION 10. Without prior approval of the City Council, the Successor Agency

ISSUE
Approve Agreement No. A-7535, with Raimi + Associates, for consulting services on the
comprehensive Zoning Ordinance Amendment (ZOA) in the amount of $500,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-7535, with Raimi + Associates, for consulting services
  on the comprehensive ZOA.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-7535,
  with Raimi + Associates, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
On June 17, 2020, the Palmdale City Council adopted Resolution NO. CC 2020-077
authorizing the application and receipt of Local Early Action Planning (LEAP) Grant funds
in the amount of $500,000. LEAP grant funds are administered by the Department of
Housing and Community Development (HUD).  On November 17, 2020, the
City of Palmdale received an award letter from HUD for the full $500,000 to use towards
a comprehensive ZOA(Palmdale Municipal Code Title 17).

The City is currently working on its first comprehensive General Plan Update in over
27 years. In order to ensure the City’s development regulations and processes are
consistent with the updated General Plan and the minimum requirements of
California State law as well as the mixing of uses, which are envisioned in the
General Plan Update, a comprehensive ZOA is required. This ZOA will contain specific
criteria for as many commonly identified land uses as possible to eliminate or minimize
the need for discretionary review, thereby reducing the time associated with the
processing of development applications. Where discretionary approval is needed, land

process.

Currently, Raimi + Associates is leading the consultant team for the General Plan Update.
They have familiarity with the City and will be able to complete the ZOA concurrently with
the General Plan Update, thereby reducing the overall project timeframe and minimizing
any potential gaps between approval of the General Plan Update and the ZOA.
Therefore, the recommended consultant is Raimi + Associates.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no impact to the General Fund by approving this agreement. The full $500,000
will be paid for by HUD through LEAP grant funds. The City is not required to provide an
in-kind or cash match under the LEAP program.

1.1  The City hereby engages CONSULTANT, and CONSULTANT accepts such

following project objectives:

·  Comprehensively update the Zoning Code (Title 17) to implement the land use
patterns, especially mixed use, and development framework established by the
Palmdale 2045 General Plan Update.

·  Prepare an updated zoning map that implements the General Plan land use
designations and is consistent with the proposed zoning districts.

·  Create a highly illustrated Code that is easy to understand and clearly conveys
the intent of the regulations with graphics, photos, and illustrations.

·  Update the development processes and procedures contained within the Zoning
Code such that these are consistent with and conform to the minimum requirements
of California State law, allow for streamlining and greatly reduce the need for
discretionary review.

·  Incorporate and build upon significant ongoing and recently completed work on

Task 3: Zoning Code Update

Task 3.1: General Plan Consistency Memo (part of the Palmdale 2045 scope)

As part of the Palmdale 2045 General Plan Update scope and budget, R+A will

include a technical review of the City’s existing zoning regulations to identifying

Task 3.2: Zoning Code Audit

Technical Review. With oversight from R+A, LWC will lead a technical review of Title
17, Palmdale Zoning Code, and related documents. The purpose of this review is to
analyze the effectiveness of the existing regulations to implement the General Plan’s
goals, objectives, and recommendations; understand the relevancy of other City
planning documents; and identify conflicts with applicable requirements of State and
federal law.

Work Session #1 with City Staff. R+A and LWC will conduct a work session with City

to assist in clarifying needed areas of updating. This will inform the preparation of the

Zoning Code Diagnosis Memo. R+A and LWC will prepare a Zoning Code Diagnosis

memo will discuss General Plan direction for new development controls, assess the
strengths and weaknesses of the existing Code, and identify key issues to be
addressed in the update and best practice recommendations for addressing the
issues. A draft Zoning Code Diagnosis Memo will be prepared for staff review and
revised based on staff comments.

BACKGROUND
The Consolidated Plan programs are formula block grant programs through the U. S.
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The City of Palmdale (City) is an
entitlement city for the purpose of determining its eligibility to receive an annual allocation
of the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program funds and a participating
jurisdiction for HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds. In addition, the

City received HUD grants for the Community Development Block Grant Coronavirus
(CDBG-CV) and Neighborhood Stabilization Program (NSP).
To assist with compliance of federal regulations for the City’s Consolidated Plan grant
programs, the City has contracted with a consultant for technical assistance for well over
ten years. The technical assistance provided has been invaluable, especially throughout
this past year. In response to COVID-19 pandemic the City received a special allocation
of $1,932,895 in CDBG-CV funds. The funds came with an array of new regulations, as
well as new guidance, waivers, and suspensions to existing Consolidated Plan Programs.
Having a high caliber and efficient technical assistant provider helps staff maintain
compliance with federal regulations and utilize Consolidated Plan Programs to respond
to the needs of the City.
DISCUSSION
The City released Request for Proposal No. 21-001-1901 on April 22, 2021, with an
estimated available budget of $300,000 billed on a time and material basis. The
notification of the RFP release was sent electronically to 328 registered vendors in the
City’s PlanetBids vendor database. On May 24, 2021 one proposal was received from
LDM Associates, Inc. (Rancho Cucamonga, CA).
The RFP 21-001-1901 criteria used for evaluating proposals were (1) Company
Experience, (2) Key Personnel, (3) Cost proposal, (4) Technical Approach. The proposal
was evaluated by two staff from Community Programs Division and one staff from the
Housing Division. Staff determined that the proposal met the RFP criteria and

1  DESCRIPTION OF WORK

1.1  The City hereby engages CONSULTANT, and CONSULTANT accepts such
engagement, to provide the following services:

In the provision of technical assistance and support to City Staff in the administration
and implementation of U. S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
Consolidated Grant programs including but not limited to the Community
Development Block Grant (CDBG), Community Block Grant Coronavirus (CDBG-
CV), Home Investment Partnerships Program (HOME), and Neighborhood
Stabilization Program (NSP). Technical assistance services are funded by the City of
Palmdale’s CDBG (Catalogue of Federal Domestic Assistance Number (CFDA)
14.218), HOME (CFDA 14.239), and NSP (CFDA 14.218) grant programs.

LDM Associates, Inc. shall provide staffing and other resources required to perform
the following scope of work as related to each specific program, as follows:

CDBG, CDBG-CV AND HOME PROGRAMS:
• Provide technical assistance for the administration of the City’s CDBG, CDBG-CV
and HOME funded Programs.
• Research regulations and best practices and answer technical inquiries regarding
eligibility of proposed activities.
• Work with City staff to determine project eligibility along with monitoring of programs
to assure compliance with all Federal, State, and Local reporting requirements.
• Work with City staff to prepare reports, as required by HUD, including but not limited

  Concord - Document ID: generated after first signature  1-14
 to One-Year Action Plan and annual funding application, annual performance report
(CAPER), Quarterly Cash Transaction Reports, Quarterly Performance Reports,
HOME Match report, Section 3, Minority and Women Owned Business Reports.
• Train staff or input into HUD’s IDIS, SPEARS and HEROS reporting systems as
needed.
• Provide technical assistance on IDIS records, including set up and preparation of
requested and required reports, preparing draw down requests for reimbursement of
expended funds, and training staff as directed.
• Coordinate with HUD field office staff and other City representatives on CDBG,
CDBG-CV and HOME related issues as needed.
• Work with City staff to prepare funding plans, administrative plans, and/or draft
guidelines for CDBG, CDBG-CV and HOME funded activities as required by HUD.
• Provide assistance, as needed, in the Administration of contracts for CDBG, CDBG-
CV and HOME funded activities, including review and process of project invoices.
• Monitor all projects for audit preparation and as required by HUD prior to close out.
• Coordinate with City staff in identification, management, and completion of all
CDBG, CDBG-CV and HOME funded projects, including preparation and review of
federal funding requirements as part of requests for proposals, monitoring reports,
public notices, etc.
• Review completed projects for all necessary compliance issues.
• Preparation of necessary Environmental Review forms and documents for CDBG,
CDBG-CV and HOME projects.
• Provide Davis-Bacon, Section 3, and MBE/WBE monitoring of construction projects
as required by Federal Labor Standards.
• Monitor public service subrecipients, public works capital improvement projects, and
grant administration.
• Annual monitoring of housing developments funded with Consolidated Plan Grant
funds. Initial set up of monitoring of developments may be required.
• Be available on-site, as needed, during HUD monitoring visits and external City
audits.
• Provide oral and written translation of information for the community in public
notices, at community meetings or other forums as needed in Spanish or other
languages.
• Any such other activities as required to properly administer the program.

NEIGHBORHOOD STABILIZATION PROGRAM (NSP):
Work with City staff to determine project eligibility along with monitoring of programs
to assure compliance with all Federal, State, and Local reporting requirements.
• Prepare reports, as required by HUD, including but not limited to Quarterly Cash
Transaction Reports, Quarterly Performance Reports, input into HUD’s DRGR
tracking system as directed.
• Maintain DRGR records, including set up and preparation of requested and required
reports. Prepare draw down requests for reimbursement of expended funds on a

  Concord - Document ID: generated after first signature  2-14
 quarterly basis or as directed.
• Coordinate with HUD field office staff and other City representatives on NSP related
issues as needed.
• Work with City staff to prepare funding plans and administrative plans for NSP
funded activities as required by HUD.
• Prepare and maintain Administrative files and contracts for NSP.
• Monitor all projects for audit preparation and as required by HUD prior to close out.
• Coordinate with City staff in identification, management, and completion of all NSP
funded projects, including preparation and review of federal funding requirements as
part of requests for proposals, monitoring reports, public notices, substantial and
insubstantial amendments, etc.
• Review completed projects for all necessary compliance issues.
• Preparation of necessary Environmental Review forms and documents for NSP
projects.
• Provide Davis-Bacon, Section 3, and MBE/WBE monitoring of construction projects
as required by Federal Labor Standards.
• Grant-close out processes.

Section 1.02 Recognition

hereby acknowledged by the City of Palmdale as the certified, exclusive and recognized
employee organization representing employees working in the City’s Maintenance
Division in the following classifications, consistent with Public Employment Relations
Board (PERB) Decision No. 2203-M and 2203a-M:

All regular full-time, probationary, and unbenefited part-time employees in the
Maintenance Division of the Department of Public Works (DPW) in the classifications of
Maintenance Helper, Custodian I and II, Lead Custodian, Maintenance Worker I and II,
Maintenance Lead Worker, Maintenance Specialist, Senior Maintenance Specialist,
Equipment Operator, Heavy Equipment Operator, Landscape Inspector, Collection
System Operator I and II, and Senior Collection System Operator.

A.  Elimination of Custodian Classification by Attrition: The parties agree that the
  classification of Custodian will be contracted out by attrition. When a position in
  the Custodian classification becomes vacant for any reason, the City will contract
  out that position, and the position will be eliminated from the bargaining unit. The
  parties agree in advance that City modification of the scope of services to be
  performed by the contractor and City modification of the scope of services to be
  performed by any and all remaining employees in the Custodian classification will
  not be subject to further meet and confer or bargaining processes. The Union has
  agreed to this contracting out by attrition. The City will advise the Union in writing
  when a position in the Custodian classification becomes vacant, but the Union
  agrees that it has waived any right to negotiate over the contracting out of that
  position. If the contracting out of a vacant Custodian position will cause any
  significant impact on the wages, hours, or working conditions of the employees in
  the Custodian classification, the City will so advise the Union, and the Union may
  request to meet and confer over the impact. However, the right to meet and confer
  over the impact shall in no way be interpreted as a right to meet and confer over

Section 2.01 Wages

Subject to the limitations and conditions set forth in this Section, wages will be as follows:

Effective the first day of the first full pay period following July 1, 2021, employees will
receive a three percent (3%) wage increase and a two percent (2%) cost of living increase
(COLA).

Effective the first day of the first full pay period following July 1, 2022, employees will
receive a one percent (1%) wage increase and a two percent (2%) cost of living increase
(COLA).

Effective the first day of the first full pay period following July 1, 2023, employees will
receive a one percent (1%) wage increase and a two percent (2%) cost of living increase
(COLA).

Effective the first day of the first full pay period following July 1, 2024, employees will
receive a one percent (1%) wage increase and a two percent (2%) cost of living increase
(COLA).

Effective the first day of the first full pay period following July 1, 2025, employees will
receive a two percent (2%) wage increase and a two percent (2%) cost of living increase
(COLA).

All wage increases and COLAs provided in this Section are contingent on annual sales
tax revenue not dropping more than five percent (5%) in a fiscal year compared to the

   Agreement No. A-7506

prior fiscal year. If annual sales tax revenue decreases by 5% but less than 10% from
one fiscal year to the next fiscal year, the City retains the right to downward adjust the
wage increase by one-half of a percentage point and the COLA by one-half of a
percentage point. If annual sales tax revenue decreases by 10% or more from one fiscal
year to the next fiscal year, the City retains the right to downward adjust the wage increase

Teamsters Local 911 agree to this wage and COLA reduction as long as the general

in which there is a downward adjustment.

Section 2.02 Overtime

A full-time nonexempt employee's normal workweek shall be forty (40) hours. The
schedule of work shall be established and may be modified by the appointing authority.
A nonexempt employee may be required to perform service in excess of 40 hours in a
workweek. A non-exempt employee will not work overtime without supervisorial approval.

Whenever a nonexempt employee works in excess of forty (40) hours in a workweek, the
employee will be compensated for such overtime work at the rate of one and one-half (1
1/2) times the hours worked. With the exception of holidays, overtime compensation shall
be based on hours worked, not hours paid. If accrued banked time is used during the
work week, overtime compensation will be calculated at the straight time rate. Holidays
will be included in the calculation of “hours worked” for purposes of overtime calculations.
For purposes of including holidays, the day the City observes the holiday will be
considered, and not the date of the actual holiday.

Section 2.03 Working Out of Classification

With the approval of the Human Resources Manager, the Director may assign regular
employees to a higher level classification in the case of unusual extended leaves and/or
vacancies of 15 consecutive calendar days or more as a professional growth and
developmental opportunity. The employee must meet the minimum qualifications to hold
the higher position in order to qualify for an out-of-class assignment. The assignment
may last for a maximum of six consecutive months. The Human Resources Manager
may approve extending the length of an Out-of-Class assignment. The Director must

Section 2.04 Compensatory Time Off (CTO)

Compensation earned for overtime hours worked may be granted in either compensatory
time-off (CTO) or in overtime pay at the option of the employee. Compensatory time
shall accrue at the rate it was earned (time and a half or straight time), to a maximum
amount of 120 hours.

Once an employee has accumulated 120 hours of compensatory time, the employee shall
be paid cash for all additional overtime worked until the compensatory time accumulated
falls below 120 hours.

An employee may use CTO with the prior approval of the employee's department head,
or the department head’s designee, with due regard to the employee's wishes and the
needs of the department. The City may deny a CTO request or postpone an employee's
CTO depending on the needs of the City. The CTO request will not be unreasonably
denied.

Terminated employees shall be paid accrued compensatory time. Compensatory time
may be used before the effective date of a layoff, retirement, resignation or termination.
If an employee’s sick leave has been depleted, accumulated compensatory time may be
used for sick leave purposes at the discretion of the appointing authority.

Employees are not required to exhaust CTO before using other paid leaves of absence.

  domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking).

When the need for sick leave is foreseeable, an employee must personally give the
employee's supervisor as much advance notice as possible of the need to take sick leave.
When the need for sick leave is not foreseeable, and except as otherwise required by
law, an employee must personally give their supervisor notice of the need to take sick

Section 5.04 Grievance Procedure

A grievance shall be defined as a controversy, as defined herein, between the City and
the Union or an employee or employees covered by this MOU and/or Human Resources
Rules and Regulations. Such controversy must pertain to any matter involving the
interpretation or application of any provision of this MOU and/or Human Resources Rules
and Regulations. This section does not apply to reviews of evaluation and matters of
discipline.

There shall be an earnest effort on the part of both parties to settle grievances promptly
through the steps listed below:

A.  Step One (Informal):

An employee’s grievance must be submitted to the first line supervisor or management
representative immediately in charge of the aggrieved employee within fifteen (15)
business days after the event giving rise to the grievance, or fifteen (15) calendar days
after the date that he/she should have been reasonably expected to have had knowledge
of the grievance. The supervisor or management representative will give an answer to
the employee by the end of the tenth (10) calendar days following the presentation of the
grievance and the giving of such answer will terminate Step 1.

B.  Step Two:

If the grievance is not settled at Step 1, the employee may elect to proceed to Step 2 by
reducing the grievance to writing. The written grievance shall fully state the facts
surrounding the grievance and detail the specific provision of this MOU and/or Human
Resources Rules and Regulations alleged to have been violated, signed and dated by
the employee and presented to the department head or his/her designee within ten (10)
calendar days after termination of Step 1. A copy of the grievance shall also be presented
to the Human Resources Manager by the employee. A meeting with the employee, shop
steward, and department head or his/her designee will be arranged at a mutually
agreeable location and time to review and discuss the grievance. Such meeting will take
place within ten (10) calendar days from the date the grievance is received by the
department head or his/her designee. The department head or his/her designee may

  Page 32 of 44
   Agreement No. A-7506

invite other members of management, including, but not limited to, Human Resources, to
be present at such meeting. The department head or his/her designee will give a written
reply by the end of the fifth (5) calendar day following the date of the meeting and the
giving of such reply will terminate Step 2.

C.  Step Three:

If the grievance is not settled at Step 2, the grievant may elect to proceed to Step 3 of the
grievance procedure. The grievant shall have five (5) calendar days to submit a written
appeal to the City Manager. If the Union and the City have mutually agreed that a grievant
can waive the requirements of Step 1 and/or 2, the grievant is required to also submit all
information that is required under Step 2. If the grievant has already completed Step 2
and submitted all required information, then the grievant is only required to submit the
request for appeal in writing.

The grievant or his/her Union representative and the City Manager or the appropriate
management representative shall within five (5) calendar days after the appeal from Step
2 arrange a meeting to be held at a mutually agreeable location and time to review and
discuss the grievance. Such meeting will take place within ten (10) calendar days from
the date the grievance is referred to Step 3. A decision shall be rendered within ten (10)
calendar days from the date of such meeting. The decision of the City Manager is final
and binding.

The time limits for filing a written formal grievance shall be strictly construed, but may be
extended by mutual agreement evidenced, in writing, and signed by a duly authorized
representative of the City and the grieving party. Failure of the grieving party to comply
with any of the time limits set forth hereunder shall constitute waiver and bar further
processing of the grievance. Failure of the City to comply with the time limits set forth in
this Section shall automatically move the grievance to the next level of the Grievance
Procedure. The grieving party may request the assistance of a Union representative in
presenting a grievance at any level of review or may represent him/herself.

Types of discipline include the following: suspension, involuntary demotion, reduction in

are expected to meet certain standards regarding their personal conduct and job
performance. Failure to meet such standards shall be grounds for appropriate disciplinary
action, which shall be commensurate with the seriousness of the offense, and will take
into consideration the employee’s personnel file. Progressive discipline will be used;
however, this does not preclude the City from taking disciplinary action, up to and
including termination, for an incident for which there is no prior documentation as long as
the disciplinary action is warranted and is based on just cause.

Disciplinary actions should be documented in the employee's official personnel file.

Performance deficiencies documented in the employee’s performance evaluation as
“unsatisfactory” may be the basis for disciplinary action if the employee fails to correct
those performance deficiencies within the time period designated by his/her supervisor.
To the extent possible, performance deficiencies or other causes for discipline will be
documented in the employee’s personnel file.

Upon receipt of written authorization from the employee, the City will provide the Union
with all written notices of discipline given to employees represented by Union. The written
notice of discipline will also inform the employee that he/she has the right to consult with
the Union in regards to the disciplinary action being taken.

D.  Administrative Leave

The Department Director may, in consultation with the Human Resources Manager,
verbally or in writing, cause the temporary assignment of an employee to status of
administrative leave with pay. In the event of a verbal notice, the Human Resources
Manager or Department Director will confirm the action by giving the employee written
notice. The employee will be advised of all restrictions to which he/she is subject to during
the period of administrative leave. If and when the employee is to return to duty, the City
will provide the employee with written notice of when he/she should return to duty, a copy
of which will be retained in the employee’s permanent personnel file.

This action may be taken at any time and for such length of time as the appointing
authority deems necessary or appropriate under the circumstances. The appointing
authority may implement an administrative leave for any legitimate reason, as determined
by the Department Director in the exercise of his or her sole discretion. Such reasons
include, but are not limited to: (1) protecting the safety or health of an employee or of
employees; (2) preventing disruption of or damage to City programs or operations; (3)
investigating alleged misconduct, including alleged harassment, by an employee; (4)
investigating an employee’s job performance; and (5) protecting the best interests of the

E.  Disciplinary Procedures

The following procedures shall be taken prior to the dismissal, suspension, involuntary
demotion, or reduction in pay of any employee for disciplinary reasons.

  1. Written Notice of Intent to Discipline (“Skelly Notice”)

When the Department Director, in consultation with the Human Resources Division,
determines that an employee has committed an act or omission that justifies discipline,
the Department Director or his/her designee shall provide the employee with written
notice of the proposed disciplinary action. Such notice shall include:

    A statement which clearly defines the intent to take action, the proposed action
  to be taken, and the proposed effective beginning and ending time of intended
  action.

    A statement of the specific grounds and particular facts upon which the
  proposed disciplinary action will be taken.

    A copy of all written materials, reports, or documents upon which the intended
  action is based.

    A statement that the employee will be afforded the right to respond to the
  Notice of Intent, either verbally, in writing, or both within five business days
  upon receipt of the intended disciplinary action, to the designated Skelly
  Officer.

    If personally delivered, the employee’s signature on the Notice of Intent will
  acknowledge receipt of said notice by the employee. If the employee refuses
  to sign, it will be noted as such on the Notice of Intent. The signature
  documentation on the Notice of Intent will acknowledge that the employee
  received the Notice of Intent.

  2. Employee Response/Pre-Disciplinary (“Skelly”) Conference

Within five business days after the employee has been served with the Notice of Intent,
the employee will have the right to respond, verbally or in writing, at the employee’s
option, to the Skelly Officer. If, within the five business days response period, the
employee does not provide a written or verbal response, the proposed action of the City
will be considered conclusive and will take effect as set forth in the Notice of Intent. Prior
to the expiration of the five business days, the response date may be adjusted by mutual
agreement, but unreasonable delay will not be tolerated.

The employee has the right to have a representative of his or her own choosing at the
Conference.

The employee’s response will be fully considered before the City issues any final notice
of disciplinary action.

Should the Skelly Officer determine that the employee’s response warrants further
investigation, the Skelly Officer may delay the implementation or modification of the
proposed disciplinary action until such time as the further investigation is completed. In
the event the investigation produces facts that warrant more severe disciplinary action
than originally proposed, the Skelly Officer will re-implement the Written Notice of Intent

  3. Written Notice of Final Disciplinary Action

  The decision of the Skelly Officer is final and shall be imposed.

  b. If the Skelly Officer decides to revoke the disciplinary action, the Skelly Officer
  will advise the employee in writing, and the original intent to impose disciplinary

BACKGROUND
The project is the fifth phase of the North County Signal Synchronization Project. The
project includes installation of conduit, traffic signal fiber, and CCTV’s for traffic signal
synchronization on arterial corridors, installation of a new traffic signal at Avenue N and
60th Street West, and installation of a new HUB at Avenue S and Tierra Subida Avenue

Project Location:
  1. Avenue S: Tierra Subida Avenue to Parkwood Drive
  2. Avenue S: Parkwood Drive to Elizabeth Lake Road
  3. 10th Street West: Rayburn Road to Avenue S
  4. Elizabeth Lake Road: 25th Street West to Ranch Center Drive
  5. Avenue N: 55th Street West to 60th Street West

DISCUSSION
It was determined that additional biological surveys are required for a rare plant, tree, and
desert plant inventory, Mohave ground squirrel, and owl burrow assessment, in additional
to agency coordination. This additional scope of work is due because the project location
is adjacent to a Significant Ecological Area (SEA) Review.

During previous habitat mapping surveys conducted by an UltraSystems Biologist in April
2020, several sensitive natural vegetation communities were identified along the project
alignment. In addition, suitable habitat for several special-status plant and animal species
exist along the alignment, including but not limited to rare plants, such as Joshua tree
(State candidate endangered) and San Fernando Valley spineflower (State endangered),
Crotch’s bumble bee (State candidate endangered), burrowing owl (BUOW, State species
of special concern), Mohave ground squirrel and other special -status wildlife. In addition,
several jurisdictional waterways that qualify as waters of the State and/or waters of the
United States are present immediately adjacent to the project alignment. Finally,
approximately 22 proposed pull box locations are within an existing SEA of Los Angeles
County and require additional review through the SEA Technical Advisory Committee
(SEATAC) if certain resources within the SEA are impacted.

Although the project site anticipates most work to occur within the right-of-way areas, the
surveys identified protected biological resources within 500 feet of the project impact
area, especially known occurrences of Joshua Tree and California Juniper. Therefore,
compliance with the City of Palmdale’s Joshua Tree and Native Desert Vegetation
Preservation Ordinance (14.04), which includes the species protected by the California
Desert Native Plants Act (Sections 800071-800075), is required for the project. In
addition, compliance with the California Endangered Species Act, the Federal
Endangered Species Act, Clean Water Act, and Porter-Cologne Act are required for this
project.

City staff explored options for avoidance of the areas that would trigger the Significant
Environmental Areas but unfortunately determined that avoidance was not possible
without compromising the purpose of this project to close the loop from the earlier ITS
Phase I-IV projects.

In addition to the environmental scope of work increase, additional civil engineering
design services are required to be performed by the subconsultant, CASC Engineering,
outside of the original scope of services. This additional work is a result of the right of
way acquisitions at 60th Street West and Avenue N. The City requested alternative design
solutions at this intersection that was deemed beneficial to be completed at this stage of
design, as opposed to further into the right of way acquisition phase.

ISSUE
Approve Ordinance No. 1566 amending Sections 2.08.050 (“Compensation”) and
2.08.060 (“Additional Compensation for Elected Mayor”) of the Palmdale Municipal
Code increasing the compensation of the Mayor and City Council?

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Receive public testimony regarding Proposed Ordinance No. 1566; and
  2. Take action on Proposed Ordinance No. 1566.

BACKGROUND
In 2003, City Councilmember compensation was $660.00 per month. At that time,
compensation for the Mayor was $1,100.00 per month. In 2007, compensation was
increased to $759.00 for City Councilmembers and $1,265.00 for the Mayor. Since that
time, council compensation has remained unchanged.
California Government Code §36516 provides a framework for general law cities to
establish and adjust council compensation. Section 36516(a) authorizes a base salary
depending upon the population of the city and provides for increases of up to 5 percent
for each calendar year from the operative date of the last salary adjustment. The salaries
set in 2003 and 2007 were made within this framework. However, in 2009, the city of
Palmdale became a charter city. Section 600 of the Charter of the city of Palmdale
empowers the City to adopt ordinances establishing the compensation of elected
officials. As such, the City Council is not constrained by California Government Code
§36516 and may set council salaries at an amount it deems appropriate.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Proposed Ordinance No. 1566
June 15, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Proposed Ordinance No. 1566 would increase the salaries of City Councilmembers to
$1,500.00 per month. It would also increase the salary of the Mayor to $2,000.00 per
month. These increases would become effective at the beginning of the next
councilmanic term of office in 2023. Serving the community as an elected official
takes a significant amount of time to attend events, meetings, and to research and
read material to be prepared to make important decisions for the community. The City
Council has not had a raise in over thirteen years.

SUBJECT:  PUBLIC HEARING TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-057 A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  APPROVING THE PALMDALE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE AND
  REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. CC 2020-074

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057 a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale approving the Palmdale Master Fee Schedule and Repealing Resolution No.
CC 2020-074.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057 to Authorize a Citywide Fee Increase of 3.6
  Percent Based Upon the Consumer Price Index (CPI), from April 2020 to April
  2021, Effective July 1, 2021, for certain departments; and
  2. Authorize the proposed rates for Planning, Engineering, Building and Safety, in a
  biennial phase in approach; and
  3. Authorize the proposed fees and charges for Code Enforcement, Sewer, Public
  Works grading plan check and permit fees.

BACKGROUND
The State Constitution provides the authority for cities to impose user fees and
regulatory fees for services and activities, however the fees may not exceed the
estimated reasonable cost of providing the service or performing the activity.

Periodically, the City Council adopts Fee Resolutions, which 1) revise existing fees,
rates, or charges; 2) establishes new fees, rates, or charges; or 3) revise headings or
descriptive language for existing fees for the City's operating departments.

In February 2018, the City Council authorized the execution of an agreement with
Revenue & Cost Specialists, LLC to perform a Cost Allocation Plan and Citywide User
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057 Restating in its Entirety the Palmdale Fee
Schedule and Repealing Resolution No. CC 2020-074
June 15, 2021
Page 2

Fee Study to ensure that fees charged by the City are appropriate in terms of cost
recovery. The findings of the study showed that the City is not fully recovering the costs
of services and the fees proposed by the consultant were substantially higher than the
City’s current fees.

The last citywide fee schedule, adopted on July 14, 2020, incorporated an increase for
the Parks & Recreation Drytown Water Park to offset minimum wage increases and the
cost of doing business, and deferred approval of fees associated with Appeal Application
to a future City Council meeting, which was later approved on August 18, 2020.

DISCUSSION
In order to better achieve the City’s policy regarding cost recovery goals and to minimize
General Fund subsidies for services provided staff has identified inefficiencies, missing
fees and/or processes.

PLANNING
Planning Fees
With the completion of the General Plan anticipated in the first quarter of 2022, Planning
staff anticipates an increase in administrative applications such as Zoning Verifications.
This is why the Planning staff is proposing to take a three-year approach to adjusting
Planning fees. The first-year addresses more of the administrative, ministerial
applications, while year two tackles discretionary actions such as Conditional Use
Permits, Site Plan Reviews, etc; year three moves into the complex discretionary actions
and legislative acts such as Specific Plan Amendments, etc. There are also several
fees that have been combined or removed for streamlining purposes.

In order to best serve the community staff has assessed other jurisdictions fees
(Attachment D) to ensure that the City of Palmdale is still remaining customer driven and
business friendly all while reducing the amount that the City is subsidizing applications
by.

BUILDING & SAFETY
Building Permit Fees
In years past the City Council has brought to the City Staff’s attention that the format in
which the Building and Safety fees are presented to the public are convoluted and hard
to understand, with this in mind City Staff has reformatted the Building and Safety Fee
items into a table format (Attachment C). This will allow the development community
and public to estimate more easily what a potential project would cost in building fees.
Staff added several categories to the building fees to ensure fair assessment of fees.
An example of this is adding the following valuation categories:

  -  $100,001 - $300,000.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057 Restating in its Entirety the Palmdale Fee
Schedule and Repealing Resolution No. CC 2020-074
June 15, 2021
Page 3

  -  300,001 - $1 million.
  -  $1 million - $10 million; and,
  -  Over $10 million.

Currently, building permit fees are assessed for building valuation with categories up to
$300,000 with a varying fractionation. Adding the additional categories above will true
up costs for buildings with a higher valuation, ie reducing their cost.

While going through this exercise staff also identified that the valuation table used to set
building valuations for permitting (the applicant can also provide their own valuation
amount) developed by the International Code Council (ICC) currently being used is from
2007. Staff is recommending changing to the 2015 valuation table, and phasing in to
the most current 2021 ICC valuation table in future years.

PUBLIC WORKS & ENGINEERING
The current fee structure for Public Works (Traffic, Industrial Waste and Public Works
Inspection) and Engineering have not been revised since 2017. The 2018 cost study
revealed significant gaps in level of service requirements compared to actual revenue
in nearly every category. It also identified many services that were being provided with
no funding source related to fees. This resulted in a recommendation for several new
fees to reflect the provision more accurately.

Several of these new fees are related to changes in and the City’s responsibility to
enforce State Law. For example, SB 743 requires project proponents to analyze their
traffic impacts using Vehicle Miles Traveled or VMT. Its review has required significant
additional staff time and corresponding fee to ensure compliance.

Another new fee is related to the City’s “ministerial” review of Small Cell proposals for
installation within the City right of way. Several utilities have requested that the City
allow them to have an Annual Permit rather than for each occurrence. This is technically
a new fee, but the result is a replacement fee that creates a more efficient and less
costly process.

Plan check and inspection fees for grading are being incorporated into the overall
Engineering Fee Schedule and therefore Exhibit B will no longer be necessary.

SEWER CAPACITY
Sewer Capacity Fees have not been adjusted since 2017 and this year staff are
proposing to adjust by CPI alone. In 2022 the City will undertake a comprehensive
update to its Sewer Master Plan, at which time the fees will be reassessed.

NEIGHBORHOOD SERVICES
Mobile Home Space Rent Control Fees
Ordinance 1531 amending Chapter 5.44 of the Palmdale Municipal Code relating to
Mobile Home Space Rent Control, passed November 5, 2019, states that any registration
submitted to the City shall be submitted with a registration fee. In 2009, the registration
fee collected from Mobile Home Parks subject to the Space Rent Control Ordinance was
$100.00 per park. At some point, the registration fee was removed from the Fee
Resolution, and subsequently the fee has not been collected.

The most recent Cost of Service Study, conducted by the City in 2018, found that Housing
Division Staff spend approximately 263 hours per year to administer the Mobile Home
Space Rent Control Ordinance. As of January 1, 2021 with the passing of state law
AB2782, spaces previously exempt from the local ordinance will be transitioning to rent
control spaces, increasing the staff time required to monitor compliance. Research of
mobile home rent control registration fees of several Southern California jurisdictions
determined that most of the jurisdictions surveyed charge fees based on the number of
spaces occupied and subject to their ordinance.

Staff recommends an annual registration fee of $5.00 per space occupied and subject to
the City’s Ordinance. This amount will not fully cover the cost to administer the Mobile
Home Space Rent Control Ordinance but will not be burdensome while re-establishing
the fee for the monitoring of compliance.

CODE ENFORCEMENT
As a result of the cost study conducted in December 2018, it is recommended to
increase the Code Enforcement fees accordingly.

The increase will support and recapture the actual cost of services related to code
enforcement action taken when property owners/agents are non-responsive to the City’s
demand to abate violations of the Palmdale Municipal Code, including Health and Safety
violations. The current fees have not been adjusted for a least fourteen years.

PARKING PENALTY SCHEDULE
As a result of the cost study conducted in December 2018, it is recommended to
increase the Parking Penalty Schedule accordingly. During the study, in an effort to
determine an equitable “proposed base penalty,” the City of Lancaster and Los Angeles’
base penalty amounts were used as comparable comparisons.

It should be noted that a portion of the fees collected on each citation is due and paid to
the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles Revenue Management –
Parking Revenue as required per Government Code 76000, 76100, 76101, 70372, and
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057 Restating in its Entirety the Palmdale Fee
Schedule and Repealing Resolution No. CC 2020-074
June 15, 2021
Page 5

Penal Code Sections 1465.5 and 1463.28; the average amount of outgoing funds is
$6,000 per month.

The current fees have not been adjusted since FY 2011/12. Additionally, The City of
Palmdale is in compliance with Assembly Bill No. 3277, which ensures that a payment
plan is available for indigent persons. The appropriate link is readily accessible both in
our office and on the City’s website.

CONCLUSION
Any action by the City to levy a new fee or service charge or to approve an increase in
an existing fee or service must be approved by ordinance or resolution. Before any new
fee or service charge can be added to the Palmdale Fee Resolution, a public hearing
must be held, and reasonable notice must be provided to the members of the
community.

Staff believes that it is important to adjust fees on a regular basis in order to keep pace
with inflation, and to avoid a growing General Fund subsidies for services provided.

As such, Staff recommends that the City Council Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-057
and Repeal Resolution No. CC 2020-074, authorizing a Citywide Fee Increase of 3.6%
based upon the CPI from April 2020 to April 2021, for certain fees, and increases as
proposed by departments as set forth in the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees
for Service, effective July 1, 2021.

PUBLIC NOTICE PROCESS
A Public Hearing Notice regarding the citywide fee resolution was published in the local
newspaper of general circulation on June 1, 2021, June 8, 2021, and again on June 14,
2021, at which time the public was invited to make oral and written presentation as part
of the regularly scheduled meeting prior to the adoption of Resolution No. CC 2021-057.
Additionally, written notice has been provided to interested parties at least 14 days prior
to the public meeting to any interested party who filed written requests for mailed notice
of meeting on new or increased development related fees or service charges.

FISCAL IMPACT
Resolution No. CC 2021-057, if adopted, would allow citywide fees to be adjusted at
the same rate of progress as inflation, and to avoid a growing General Fund subsidies
for services provided.

   City Council Staff Report
DATE:  JUNE 15, 2021
TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
FROM:  CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE
DISTRICT:  ALL
SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-062 A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE INCREASING THE
  VEHICLE ALLOWANCE RECEIVED BY THE MAYOR AND CITY
  COUNCILMEMBERS FROM $200 MONTHLY TO $500 MONTHLY

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-062 a Resolution of the City of Palmdale Increasing the
Vehicle Allowance Received by the Mayor and City Councilmembers from $200 monthly
to $500 monthly.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Discuss and establish a vehicle allowance in an amount that is “reasonably related
  to what is required for the performance of the City Councilmembers’ public duties;”
  and
  2. If the City Council determines that $500 is “reasonably related to what is required
  for the performance of the City Councilmembers’ public duties,” adopt Resolution
  No. CC 2021-062 a Resolution of the City of Palmdale Increasing the Vehicle
  Allowance Received by the Mayor and City Councilmembers as drafted.

BACKGROUND
The City Council is authorized, pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.070,
to “receive a vehicle allowance, at the end of each calendar month, without the necessity
of presentation of an itemized accounting, receipts, vouchers or other documentation.”
The amount of the vehicle allowance is set by resolution of the City Council and must be
“reasonably related to what is required for the performance of the City Councilmembers’
public duties.” The current vehicle allowance, effective since March 2001, is $200 per
month. The City Council discussed the existing vehicle allowance at the March 16th City
Council meeting and directed Staff to prepare a resolution increasing the vehicle
allowance to $500 per month.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-062 a Resolution of the City of Palmdale Increasing
the Vehicle Allowance Received by the Mayor and City Councilmembers
June 15, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
State law authorizes cities to adopt vehicle allowances for city councilmembers.
Specifically, California Government Code Section 1223 provides that, “[w]hen traveling
expenses are allowed by law to any state, county, judicial district, or city officer, he may
contract with the appropriate authorities for an allowance or mileage rate for the use of
vehicles owned or rented and used by him in the performance of duty, in lieu of the usual
transportation charges.” In addition, the Attorney General has opined that “a city may
provide a vehicle allowance to its city council members in lieu of reimbursing actual
vehicle expenses after such expenses are incurred.” See 93 Ops.Cal.Atty.Gen. 9.

Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.070 authorizes the Mayor and City
Councilmembers to receive a vehicle allowance and requires that the amount be
“reasonably related to what is required for the performance of the City Councilmembers’
public duties.” Proposed Resolution CC 2021-062 makes a finding that a vehicle
allowance in the amount of $500 is reasonably related to what is required for the
performance of the City Councilmembers’ public duties and sets a new vehicle
allowance in that amount. The new vehicle allowance will be effective July 1, 2021. If
the City Council believes that the amount of $500 reflects the reasonable monthly cost
to use a personal vehicle for City Council business, the City Council should adopt
Resolution CC 2021-062.

FISCAL IMPACT
Adoption of Proposed Resolution CC 2021-062 would increase the annual cost to the City
for vehicle allowances by $18,000.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  A. Manage resources, costs and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-062

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  INCREASING THE VEHICLE ALLOWANCE RECEIVED BY THE MAYOR
  AND CITY COUNCILMEMBERS

  WHEREAS, The City Council has determined that efficiency would be served by
receiving reimbursement for vehicle expenses at the end of each calendar month
without the necessity of presentation of an itemized accounting, receipts, vouchers or
other documentation, and that costs associated with use of a personal vehicle, such as
fuel, maintenance, and insurance, periodically increase; and

  WHEREAS, Palmdale Municipal Code 2.08.070 authorizes the City Council to
receive a vehicle allowance in an amount, established by resolution of the City
Council, that is “reasonably related to what is required for the performance of the City
Councilmembers’ public duties;” and

  WHEREAS, The City Council determined in 1989 that the minimum expenses
for the use of a personal vehicle actually and necessarily incurred by each City
Councilmember in performance of official duty to be at least $100.00 per month and
established a vehicle allowance in that amount; and

  WHEREAS, In 2001, the City Council, citing increased fuel and operating costs,
increased the vehicle allowance to $200 per month; and

  WHEREAS, The vehicle allowance has not changed in two decades, however,
the costs associated with the use of a personal vehicle, such as fuel, maintenance,
and insurance, have significantly increased; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council has determined that the amount of $500.00 is
reasonably related to what is required for the performance of the City
Councilmembers’ public duties.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The City Council hereby specifically finds that all the facts set forth
in the Recitals of this Resolution are true and correct.
